newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close mixed, yield curve steepens.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close mixed, yield curve steepens.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed mixed on Monday with a stronger dollar prompting the yield curve to steepen as trading volumes were kept low by the absence of a U.S. market, dealers said.

"The only real bias to the curve has been a steepening bias. We've seen the short end pick up some support from the Canadian dollar," said Andrew Pyle, head of fixed-income research with ABN-AMRO Bank Canada.
Canada's 30-year bond fell C$0.16 to C$108.19 to yield 7.295 percent. The U.S. 30-year bond last traded with a yield of 6.82 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds widened to 48 basis points from 45 basis points at the close of trading on Friday.

Canada's dollar rallied to as high as C$1.3353 (US$0.7488) during the session, providing support for short-term issues even as long bond prices drifted lower. Trading was light in most Canadian financial markets with U.S. fixed-income markets closed for Martin Luther King day. Dealers said there had been talk of an early close but it never materialized.
Analysts said bond investors are now looking ahead to testimony tomorrow morning by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan for clues on the next move in U.S. rates.
Investors are also looking ahead to the release of economic data later this week, including Canadian retail sales for November on Wednesday and the consumer price index for December on Thursday.
The market is also awaiting the auction of C$1.3 billion 30-year Government of Canada bonds on Wednesday, analysts said.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 fell C$0.10 to C$102.80 to yield 6.607 percent.
The U.S. 10-year bond last traded with a yield of 6.55 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds widened to six basis points from three basis points at Friday's close.
The three-month cash bill traded with a yield of 2.78 percent against the U.S. bill which last yielded 5.15 percent.
